hardening_shipped: FORBID_TAGS ['style'] on every markdown/html sanitise path (pre-existing page-global CSS injection through DOMPurify's default tag list — found by the engineering review, fixed here, pinned in sanitizeHooks.spec.js and markdownCodeBlocks.spec.js)
Canvas mode: class allowlist (exact KIT_CLASSES membership), style allowlist (width/max-width, % ≤ 100, px ≤ 9999), id forbidden

findings.title: Kit root did not contain an admitted inline width; a width up to 9999px could widen the page
findings.exploit: An agent (or a prompt-injected agent) writes an html block with style="width: 9999px" on a roster canvas; the Workspace page of every rostered customer gains a horizontal scrollbar and the header/rail push off-screen. No data exposure.
findings.impact: Product-bar violation (principle 7), not a disclosure — but it lands on a customer-facing page.
findings.recommendation: Applied in this PR: `.canvas-kit { overflow-x: auto }`, pinned by test_ent537_canvas_design_kit.py::test_the_kit_root_contains_its_own_overflow.

findings.title: themeCSS init directive reaching the page through the SVG <style> that sanitizeSvg keeps
findings.exploit: Claimed: %%{init: {"themeCSS": "body{display:none}"}}%% in diagram source → global CSS. Refuted by an independent verifier on mermaid 11.16.1: compileCSS namespaces every rule under #<diagram-id> (mermaid.core.mjs:1145-1203), so the selector matches nothing. Residual: @keyframes are left un-namespaced and could redefine an app animation name (visual nuisance only).
findings.impact: None for the claim; cosmetic for the residual.
findings.recommendation: Applied in this PR as hardening: MERMAID_CONFIG.secure = ['themeCSS','fontFamily','altFontFamily'] so mermaid's sanitize() deletes them from any directive; pinned in canvasUtils.spec.js.
